items.title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders 

A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it.

Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest.

New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday.

“Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.”

Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from 

The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state.

Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million.

items.title: Spain Lets Anti-Money Laundering Unit Freeze Crypto Accounts Without a Judge
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Spain Lets Anti-Money Laundering Unit Freeze Crypto Accounts Without a Judge 

Spain has given its financial intelligence unit the power to freeze crypto accounts on its own authority, without first getting a judge’s approval, when it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing.

The change was published in Spain’s official state gazette on Wednesday as part of Royal Decree-Law 44/2026, a sweeping decree that mostly deals with consumer credit contracts and the sale of bad loan portfolios. Its sixth final provision adds a new Article 46 bis to the country’s 2010 anti-money laundering law.

The new article lets the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offenses, known as Sepblac, suspend or refuse to authorize a transaction in progress. It can also suspend the use of a bank, payment or crypto-asset account, or a business relationship, when there are “indications” that it could be tied to money laundering or terrorist financing.

According to the text, the goal is to preserve the funds while Sepblac carries out its analysis and checks whether the suspicion holds up. If it does, the unit passes the information to the competent authorities so they can take further action.

Five days for accounts, 10 for transactions 

The decree sets two separate time limits. Sepblac can hold a pending transaction for no more than 10 business days, and it can freeze an account or business relationship for no more than five. Either hold must be lifted sooner if it is no longer needed to preserve the funds.

items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally 

The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November.

The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets.

Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift.

Tech futures lead the risk rebound 

Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%.

“There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008.

items.title: Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June 

Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.”

Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.”

The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case.

That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets.

Galaxy points to $58,525 

The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22.

Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by…

items.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally 

The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter).

Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus .

Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits.

The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed…
items.t: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
